name: Puri Khaja
instructions: 1. Mix flour, a little melted ghee, and salt with water to form a firm dough and let it rest for 30 minutes.
2. Divide the dough into small balls and roll them into very thin circular sheets.
3. Apply a mixture of ghee and flour paste (sata) on each sheet, stack them, and roll them tightly into a cylindrical log.
4. Cut the log into small pieces (khajas) and gently press them down with a rolling pin.
5. Deep-fry the pieces in medium-hot oil until golden brown and crispy.
6. Prepare a one-string consistency sugar syrup flavored with cardamom.
7. Dip the fried khajas into the warm syrup until coated well and let them dry to form a sugary glaze.
description: Puri Khaja is a traditional sweet delicacy from the holy city of Puri, Odisha. It is famously known as a key 'Chhappan Bhog' (56 offerings) presented to Lord Jagannath at the Jagannath Temple. Its unique multi-layered, crispy texture and sugar-soaked finish make it a cultural icon of Odia confectionery.
